# Ben Android Builds

Each row is a debug-signed APK produced by `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` or
`./gradlew assembleDebug` and copied here. Filename convention:

```
Ben-<versionName>-<gitShortSHA>[-dirty]-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.apk
```

The actual `.apk` files are gitignored (they're ~85 MB each); only this
changelog ships in the repo.

| `Ben-0.1.4-728f461-dirty-20260507-1915.apk` | 2026-05-07 19:15 | 0.1.4 | `728f461` (dirty) | **Durable on-device memory parity with Mac.** The Mac side has had OpenClaw's `memory_search` / `memory_get` / `memory_*` tool family + a hand-curated `USER.md` from day one; Android did not, which is why the user could ask "biryani like last Friday" or "send to my home address" and get nothing useful. (1) **`memory.*` tools**: `memory.set({key, value, tags?})`, `memory.get({key})`, `memory.search({query?, tag?, limit?})`, `memory.list({prefix?, limit?})`, `memory.delete({key})`. JSON-backed store at `<workspace>/memory.json` with atomic tmp+rename writes, in-process mtime-keyed cache, 16 KB-per-entry cap, optional tag-based grouping. Empty-query search returns most-recently-updated entries so the model can probe "what do I know about this user". (2) **`memory.user_facts` + `memory.append_user_facts`**: read / append the canonical `USER.md` file the user can hand-edit. The model uses `append_user_facts` for long-term identity ("my home is at 21 Whitefield"), `memory.set` for keyed state ("home_address" -> ...) and one-off snapshots ("last_swiggy_order"). (3) **Auto-injected session context**: new `session.context` JSON-RPC method on the inbound bridge bundles `USER.md` + the 8 most-recently-updated memory facts and returns them in one round-trip. `BenVoiceService.connect()` calls it synchronously (parallel to `tools.list`) and prepends two new sections — `USER FACTS:` and `RECENT MEMORIES:` — to the system prompt. The model now sees the user's name, contacts, addresses, payment defaults, and recent saved facts at every wake without having to ask. (4) **System prompt update**: documents the seven new tools and adds a `MEMORY DISCIPLINE` clause — treat USER FACTS as authoritative, persist new long-term facts via `memory.append_user_facts`, prefer `memory.search` over asking the user for data they may already have given you. Total tool count is now **31** (was 24). (5) **Tests**: `automation_simulation.test.js` now has an 8th scenario covering the full memory round-trip (set, get with tags, search by value substring, search-by-key outscoring search-by-value, tag filter, list, delete, USER.md append + read-back, full `session.context` envelope assertion). All passing. Other test suites unchanged and still green (`tools_rpc` 11 tools; `wake_phrase_matcher` 38/38; `kotlin_rpc` 10 methods). |
| `Ben-0.1.3-ba33c02-dirty-20260507-1840.apk` | 2026-05-07 18:40 | 0.1.3 | `ba33c02` (dirty) | User-reported regressions: wake word does not fire ("notification says listening but Ben does literally nothing"), weather/reminders/alarms cannot be set, conversation cuts off after 3 s of silence. (1) **Wake recognizer reliability** — `EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE` is now set initially but flipped off after **2** consecutive recoverable errors (`ERROR_NO_MATCH` / `ERROR_SPEECH_TIMEOUT` / `ERROR_LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED` / `ERROR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE`), so phones without an offline en-US pack — the most likely root cause of the silent-failure mode — now fall back to the network recogniser automatically. Every `onError(...)` is now logged with its symbolic name (e.g. `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS (RECORD_AUDIO not granted!)`). (2) **WakePhraseMatcher v0.1.3 rule** — short tokens (length < 4, e.g. "Ben") now allow 1 Damerau-Levenshtein edit IF the first character matches. Catches "ben"/"bend"/"bin"/"ban"/"been" (which Android `SpeechRecognizer` returns far more often than the bare word "ben") but still rejects "pen"/"hen"/"ten"/"len". 4-6 char tokens stay exact. 7+ char tokens stay 1-edit. Mirrored across Kotlin / JS / Python; all three test suites pass (38/38 each). (3) **Mic Test diagnostic screen** — new `MicTestActivity` reachable from the Home tab. Shows live transcripts of every event the recogniser emits (READY / BEGIN / PARTIAL / RESULT / WAKE_MATCH / ERROR / RESTART), plus permission/battery/accessibility status with a one-tap "Open settings" jump for whichever is missing, plus a "Force restart wake listener" button that resets `preferOffline=true` and recreates the `SpeechRecognizer`. Eventbuffer is a `ConcurrentLinkedDeque` so the screen also shows pre-launch history. The user can now SEE what's broken instead of guessing. (4) **Conversation idle window** — `POST_RESPONSE_SILENCE_MS` 3 s -> 180 s (3 min) and `HARD_SESSION_CAP_MS` 180 s -> 600 s (10 min). The user explicitly asked for "at least three minutes". Server VAD `silence_duration_ms` dropped 3000 -> 1000 ms because that one is for end-of-turn detection, not end-of-session — they were conflated. (5) **New tools to make alarms/timers/reminders/weather actually work** — `device.set_alarm({hour, minute?, label?})`, `device.set_timer({seconds, label?})` (both via `AlarmClock` intents, no permission needed), `device.add_calendar_event({title, start, end?, duration_minutes?, description?, location?})` (via `CalendarContract` Insert intent — opens the calendar UI prefilled). `web.fetch({url, method?, body?, headers?})` for generic HTTPS calls (capped at 64 KB body). `weather.current({location?})` wraps wttr.in (no API key). Total registered tool count is now 24 (was 19). All wired into the system prompt with the canonical flows the model should run for "set an alarm", "remind me", "what's the weather", etc. (6) **System prompt rewrite** — explicit canonical flows for WEATHER / ALARMS / REMINDERS / ON-PHONE UI / CROSS-DEVICE; explicit "the conversation stays open for up to 3 minutes of silence between turns and 10 minutes total — do NOT close the conversation early or push the user". (7) **Defensive auto-resume window** for the wake listener bumped from 200 s -> 620 s to match the new 600 s session cap (was racing against legitimate long sessions). All 4 node test suites pass (`wake_phrase_matcher` 38/38; `kotlin_rpc` 10 methods; `tools_rpc` 11 tools; `automation_simulation` 7 scenarios, 24 tools registered, 18 Kotlin RPCs round-tripped). |
| `Ben-0.1.2-4849c4d-dirty-20260507-1753.apk` | 2026-05-07 17:53 | 0.1.2 | `4849c4d` (dirty) | Tool surface parity with Mac. Built on top of the 17:35 build. (1) **OpenClaw `ui.*` tool family** — `ui.read_screen`, `ui.click({text\|ax_id})`, `ui.click_at(x,y)`, `ui.type(text)`, `ui.scroll(direction[, amount])`, `ui.swipe(x1,y1,x2,y2)`, `ui.screenshot()`, `ui.screen_size()`, `ui.focus_app(package)`. These now mirror the Mac `mac_*` surface 1:1. `ui.click` accepts visible text (fuzzy substring match against the AccessibilityService tree) OR an exact `ax_id`. (2) **Vision tools** — `vision.locate_text(target)` runs ML Kit OCR against a fresh screenshot and returns `{found, text, confidence, score, bbox, click_x, click_y}` ready to feed into `ui.click_at` (mirrors Mac's `text_locate`). `vision.read_screen(question)` sends the screenshot to gpt-4o for multimodal Q&A (mirrors Mac's `vision_read`). Together these unlock Compose / WebView / Electron-style apps where the AX tree is sparse. (3) **System prompt rewrite** — BenVoiceService.kt now teaches the model the standard on-phone flow (launch -> read tree -> click by text/ax_id -> if miss, screenshot + vision.locate_text + click_at -> type -> tap Send -> verify). Cross-device delegation rule for "on my Mac, ..." utterances. (4) **End-to-end simulation** — new `assets/node/test/automation_simulation.test.js`: 5 scenarios, 19 tools registered, 15 Kotlin RPCs round-tripped. Drives "Open WhatsApp -> find Pragati -> type 'Hi' -> Send" against a mock kotlin RPC server, exercises the full registry/inbound/kotlin_rpc/builtin_tools chain, asserts the typed text reaches the mocked AccessibilityService and that the verification tree shows the sent message. Also exercises the vision fallback path (sparse-tree app + OCR-rich screen -> vision.locate_text returns coords -> ui.click_at advances the screen). All four node test files pass. Build size 89 MB. |
| `Ben-0.1.2-4849c4d-dirty-20260507-1735.apk` | 2026-05-07 17:35 | 0.1.2 | `4849c4d` (dirty) | Voice flow correctness + OpenClaw tool wiring. (1) **FGS crash fix**: `BenWakewordService.kt` now calls plain `startService(BenVoiceService)` instead of `startForegroundService` - 0.1.1 was raising `RemoteServiceException` ~5 s into every conversation because BenVoiceService no longer calls `startForeground()` and its manifest `foregroundServiceType` was dropped. This was the root cause of the ~30 s mid-stream cutoff and the cascading "Conversation in progress" notification miss + pairing regression. (2) **Anti-filler discipline**: `session.update` now ships `max_response_output_tokens=800` (hard 30-40 s ceiling) and the system prompt has explicit "Be concise. At most two short sentences. Do not say filler phrases like 'I'll help you with that' / 'just a moment' / 'sure thing'. After answering, stop and wait for the user." (3) **Race-free `isAssistantSpeaking`**: flag is now anchored to the response.created/response.done lifecycle (one event per turn) instead of per-chunk response.audio.done events that left stale-false windows allowing speaker output to bounce back into mic. (4) **OpenClaw tool wiring** - Phase 2 of the plan that should already have been there: `assets/node/src/openclaw/` now has a registry.js + builtin_tools.js + device_tools.js. inbound_rpc.js exposes `tools.list` and `tools.invoke` JSON-RPC methods. BenVoiceService synchronously fetches the tool registry from the Node bridge before opening the WSS and ships it in `session.update`. New `response.function_call_arguments.delta/done` handler dispatches calls on a single-thread executor (so the WSS thread isn't blocked), sends `conversation.item.create{type:function_call_output}` + `response.create` to continue. The silence timer is paused while a tool call is in flight so the model doesn't get killed mid-tool-roundtrip. (5) **Native Android device tools**: `device.get_location`, `device.get_contacts(query?)`, `device.place_call({number\|contact_name})`, `device.launch_app({package\|label})`, `device.clipboard_get/set`, `device.battery_status`. Implemented in `AndroidDeviceBridge.kt`; routed through NodeBridgeService's RPC handler map. Plus `peer.delegate({task})` for "on my Mac, ..." cross-device handoff and `ax.tap_text` / `ax.type_text` / `ax.screenshot` for in-app UI automation. (6) **Permission gate**: `PermissionGateActivity` (translucent shim) is fired when a tool returns `permission_not_granted`; the user grants access in the system dialog and re-issues the voice command. (7) **Live wake phrase in UI**: `home_status_idle` is now a `%1$s` format string. HomeFragment formats with `BenSecrets.wakePhrase` on view-create + on resume + on a `WAKE_PHRASE_CHANGED` LocalBroadcast from SettingsActivity. The Home screen used to literally say "Idle. Say 'Ben' to start." regardless of the user's actual setting. (8) **Incremental history**: SessionStore now writes a per-session `_live/<sessionId>.json` snapshot on each turn (debounced 500 ms) so the History UI can show in-progress sessions; on session end the snapshot is unlinked and the canonical `index.jsonl` row is appended. (9) **AndroidManifest.xml**: added ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, READ_CONTACTS, CALL_PHONE permissions and registered `PermissionGateActivity` with translucent theme. (10) Tests: new `node test/tools_rpc.test.js` round-trips tools.list and tools.invoke against a mock OpenClaw registry + fake Kotlin device server; existing wake_phrase_matcher and kotlin_rpc tests still pass. Build size 89 MB, same ABIs as 0.1.1. |
| `Ben-0.1.1-4849c4d-dirty-20260507-1631.apk` | 2026-05-07 16:31 | 0.1.1 | `4849c4d` (dirty) | Comprehensive runtime bug bundle. (1) OpenAI Realtime session.update now hard-locks English: explicit "always reply in English, never reply in any other language" instruction clause + `input_audio_transcription{model:whisper-1, language:en}` + `turn_detection{type:server_vad, silence_duration_ms:3000}`. (2) Mic uploads suppressed while assistant is speaking - kills the speaker -> mic feedback loop that produced the Hindi storm. (3) After every model `response.done` we wait 3 s of silence then `stopAndRearm()`; user must say wake phrase again to re-enter conversation. (4) Stop intents ("stop", "shut up", "i'm not talking to you", "cancel", etc.) detected from user transcripts immediately end the session. (5) Hard 180 s cap as runaway guard. (6) `BenVoiceService` no longer posts its own foreground notification - the lone `BenForegroundService` notification (id 4711) flips text from idle to active, so the duplicate "Conversation in progress" entry is gone. (7) Idle notification now reads `Listening for "<wake_phrase>"` from `BenSecrets` (was hardcoded to "Ben" regardless of user setting). (8) Wake listener `wantsRestart` flag now correctly resets on `ACTION_RESUME`, plus a 200 s defensive auto-resume timer in case `BenVoiceService` crashes silently. (9) `WakePhraseMatcher` strict-match threshold raised from <=4 to <=6 chars: "Ben"/"Sasha"/"Jarvis"/"Friday" now all require exact match, killing "tasha"/"saska"/"jarviz"/"frida" false-positive triggers. (10) Pairing UX: 1500-1800 px PNG QR (was ~600 px), explicit CAMERA runtime permission grant, "Paste pairing URI" button reading clipboard for camera-less pairing, and the existing `jarvis://pair` deep link via `PairingDeepLink` activity-alias. |
